title_en: Shanghai Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Intellectual Property Office — dispute over the decision on patent infringement
ruling_gist_en: When hearing an administrative case concerning a decision on handling a patent infringement dispute, a people's court shall, in light of the trial characteristics of civil cases regarding patent infringement disputes, on the basis of conducting a comprehensive legality review, focus on examining whether the facts concerning the manufacture and sale of the allegedly infringing products as determined in the decision on handling the patent infringement dispute are objective and accurate.
keywords_en: administrative; decision on handling a patent infringement dispute; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; legal person; state organ; Patent Law; determination of facts of patent infringement; legality of administrative decision; patent infringement dispute; administrative handling decision; administrative litigation; intellectual property rights; patent infringement dispute of the Municipal Intellectual Property Office
full_text_en:
Shanghai Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Intellectual Property Bureau — patent infringement dispute handling decision

Ruling Summary

When trying an administrative case concerning a decision on handling a patent infringement dispute, a people's court shall, based on the characteristics of the trial of civil cases concerning patent infringement disputes and on the basis of conducting comprehensive legality review, focus on reviewing whether the facts identified in the decision on handling the patent infringement dispute regarding the manufacture and sale of the allegedly infringing product are objective and accurate.

Plaintiff: Shanghai Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1, Zhongshan North First Road, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Wei Wei, Chairman of the Board.
Defendant: Shanghai Intellectual Property Bureau, domiciled at No. 1, Jumu Road, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Lü Guoqiang, Director of the Bureau.
Third Party: Shanghai Jia Dong Li Environmental Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 1, Manufacturing Bureau Road, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Ge Yongle, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Quanneng Company), dissatisfied with the Decision on Handling Patent Infringement Dispute No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22 (沪知局处字〔2008〕第22号) made by the defendant, Shanghai Intellectual Property Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Shanghai IP Bureau), filed an administrative lawsuit with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court. The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held that Shanghai Jia Dong Li Environmental Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jia Dong Li Company) had a legal interest in the case and added it as a third party to participate in the proceedings.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff alleged that it had never manufactured or sold any product without a standard designation that violated the *Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China* and was named "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" (Patent No. ZL200510029351.6). The decision on handling the patent infringement dispute made by the defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, was inconsistent with the facts. The plaintiff, pursuant to a license from a non-party, Ningbo Rongsheng Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rongsheng Company), practiced the utility model patent (Patent No. ZL200720106248.1) and the design patent (Patent No. ZL200730110936.0) for the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer," and operated the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" product, which should be protected by law. The technology used by the plaintiff was based on publicly known technology and was innovative; the product produced predated the third party's product and differed from the third party's patent or product in structure, name, trademark, etc. The plaintiff contended that the decision on handling the patent infringement dispute made by the defendant contained improper findings of fact, erroneous application of law, and illegal enforcement procedures. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the revocation of the Decision on Handling Patent Infringement Dispute No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22 made by the Shanghai IP Bureau on June 19, 2009.

The plaintiff, Quanneng Company, submitted the following three groups of evidentiary materials:

First Group of Evidence:
1. Operating principle of the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" product. This evidence was meant to illustrate the working principle of the plaintiff's product, that aspects identical to the third party, Jia Dong Li Company's, invention patent were all publicly known, while the differing aspects were the plaintiff's own creations.
2. Utility model patent specification for "Control Circuit Device of Atomizing Cooling Type Air Conditioner Atomizing Device," Patent No. ZL200520044748.8.
3. Utility model patent specification for "Water Spray Cooling Split Air Conditioner," Patent No. ZL200520040406.9.
4. Publication specification of the invention patent application for "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners," Patent Application No. 200510029351.6.
   Evidence 2-4 was intended to demonstrate irregularities in the said patent applications.
5. Inspection report from the Shanghai Product Quality Supervision and Inspection Institute. This evidence was intended to show that the third party's product was a household air conditioner of specification JDL-35GW and was unrelated to the product operated by the plaintiff.
6. Utility model patent specification for "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer," Patent No. ZL200720106248.1.
7. Design patent certificate for "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer," Patent No. ZL200730110936.0.
8. Inspection report from the Shanghai Institute of Quality Supervision and Inspection Technology.
9. Patent fee receipt.
10. Trademark registration application form, contract, and application acceptance notice.
11. Acceptance notice for the application for registration of the "Li Neng" (立能) trademark.
12. 2007 Ningbo City Industrial New Product Plan Project Application Form, and the 2007 Ningbo City First Batch of Industrial New Product Trial Production Plan Project Summary Table.
13. Copy of patent agent's business card.
14. Non-party Rongsheng Company's enterprise standards for brushless DC motors and air conditioner atomizers, and materials for the filing of the technical service agreement.
15. Intellectual property transfer entrustment contract between Rongsheng Company and the plaintiff, and the power of attorney from Rongsheng Company.
16. Filing materials for the patent implementation license contract at the Zhejiang Province Intellectual Property Office.
17. Air conditioner energy-saving atomizer RSW5000A incoming inspection guidelines, inspection and testing regulations, control methods for non-conforming products, and inspection requirements (periodic inspection).
18. Materials from various exhibition activities of the plaintiff and Rongsheng Company since 2007, and certificates of honor.
19. Project listing service agreement with Shanghai Environment and Energy Exchange and the listing fee invoice.
20. Materials related to the notarization conducted by the plaintiff, including the notarization acceptance notice.
21. The atomizer physical item and invoice purchased by the plaintiff for evidence collection.
   Evidence 6-21 was intended to demonstrate that the products operated by the plaintiff originated from Rongsheng Company's patent authorization and were legitimately sourced.

Second Group of Evidence consisted of 23 utility model patent specifications, specifically:
1. "Electric Sprayer," Patent No. ZL96213165.2.
2. "High-Efficiency Light Agricultural Sprayer," Patent No. 200420011322.8.
3. "A Misting Machine Nozzle," Patent No. ZL200420015841.1.
4. "A Micro-Power Electric Sprayer," Patent No. ZL95228127.9.
5. "A New Type of Electric Sprayer," Patent No. ZL94242515.4.
6. "Misting Machine Nozzle," Patent No. ZL03219104.9.
7. "Air Conditioner Water Spray Energy Saver," Patent No. ZL91230083.3.
8. "Air Conditioner Condensate Atomizer," Patent No. ZL98243731.5.
9. "Air Conditioner Condenser Spray Cooling Energy Saver," Patent No. ZL02261354.4.
10. "Air Conditioner Drip Atomizer," Patent No. ZL200420011257.9.
11. "Air Conditioner Drip Atomizer," Patent No. ZL97242917.4.
12. "Air Conditioner Condensate Atomizer," Patent No. ZL03245955.6.
13. "Split Air Conditioner Condensate Sprayer," Patent No. ZL01213934.3.
14. "Treatment Device for Condensate of Air Conditioner," Patent No. ZL01130815.X.
15. "Air Conditioning and Humidifying Misting Device," Patent No. ZL93226666.5.
16. "Air Conditioner Condensate Treatment Device," Patent No. ZL97240570.4.
17. "Air Conditioner Energy Saving and Efficiency Enhancement Device," Patent No. ZL200420036205.7.
18. "Summer Air Conditioner Energy-Saving and Consumption-Reducing Condensate Treatment Device," Patent No. ZL200410055494.X.
19. "Portable Electric Sprayer," Patent No. ZL91225068.2.
20. "Portable Electric Sprayer," Patent No. ZL93204108.6.
21. "Centrifugal Sprayer," Patent No. ZL93228585.6.
22. "Condensate Collection Atomizer," Patent No. ZL99254762.8.
23. "Air Conditioner Outdoor Unit Utilizing Air Conditioner Condensate," Patent No. ZL200520030649.4.
   The above evidence was intended to prove that atomizers had long existed and were publicly known technology, and that the plaintiff, Quanneng Company's, products were manufactured based on publicly known technology.

Third Group of Evidence:
1. Comparison opinion between the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" product and the "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" product.
2. Acceptance notice for the application for registration of the "Li Neng" trademark.
3. Acceptance notice for the application for registration of the "Li Neng" trademark.
4. Trademark registration application form.
5. Filing certificate for the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" utility model patent implementation license contract.
6. Filing certificate for the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" design patent implementation license contract.
7. Power of attorney from Ningbo Runze Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. regarding the "Li Neng" trademark.
8. Power of attorney from non-party Rongsheng Company regarding the "Li Neng" trademark.
9. Intellectual property transfer entrustment contract.
10. Notarial deed obtained by the plaintiff, Quanneng Company, for preserving webpage evidence.
    The above evidence was intended to prove facts such as the implementation license of a design patent and the license to use the trademark for the allegedly infringing product.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, argued that the procedure for making the Decision on Handling Patent Infringement Dispute No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22 was lawful, the facts were clearly identified, and the law was correctly applied. The Bureau requested the court to uphold the decision.

The defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, submitted the following evidence and legal basis:

I. Evidence of the defendant's authority: Notice of the General Office of Shanghai Municipal People's Government on Printing and Issuing the Provisions on the Functions, Internal Structure, and Staffing of Shanghai Intellectual Property Bureau (Hufu Ban Fa [2000] No. 64), to prove its responsibility for lawfully handling patent disputes in Shanghai.

II. Evidence on the enforcement procedure of the specific administrative act:
1. Request for mediation of patent infringement by the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, to prove that the third party submitted a request for handling a patent infringement dispute to the defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, on September 17, 2008.
2. Acceptance notices for the handling of patent infringement dispute requests No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22002 and No. 22003; notice of defense No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22004 and service receipt; the plaintiff, Quanneng Company's, statement of defense; oral hearing notices No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22005 and No. 22006 and oral hearing receipts; oral hearing notices No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22007 and No. 22008 and oral hearing receipts; the oral hearing record of the defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, dated November 12, 2008; the Decision on Handling Patent Infringement Dispute No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22 and service receipts and domestic postal receipts. The above evidence was used to prove that after receiving the third party, Jia Dong Li Company's, request for handling a patent infringement dispute, the defendant followed procedures including case filing and acceptance, defense by the parties, oral hearing, issuance of the decision on handling the patent infringement dispute, and service of the decision on the parties, and that the enforcement procedures were lawful.

III. Evidence on the facts found in the specific administrative act:
1. Invention patent certificate for Patent No. ZL200510029351.6 and annual patent fee receipt; invention patent specification; patent implementation license contract and filing certificate for the patent implementation license contract. The above evidence was used to prove that the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, was the exclusive licensee of the invention patent No. ZL200510029351.6, that the patent was valid, and the scope of protection of that patent.
2. The physical atomizer of the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer RSW5000A"; the product manual of the plaintiff, Quanneng Company's, air conditioner energy-saving atomizer; Shanghai Commercial Uniform Invoice No. 04401068; and the plaintiff's business license. The above evidence was used to prove that the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer RSW5000A" atomizer manufactured and sold by the plaintiff covered all the essential technical features of the invention patent No. ZL200510029351.6.
3. Utility model patent specification titled "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" (Patent No. ZL200720106248.1) and design patent publication document titled "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" (Patent No. ZL200730110936.0); excerpts from 44 patent publications; the 2007 Ningbo City First Batch of Industrial New Product Trial Production Plan Project Summary Table; inspection report from the Shanghai Institute of Quality Supervision and Inspection Technology; non-party Rongsheng Company's enterprise standards for brushless DC motors and air conditioner atomizer technical service agreements; and patent publication documents for Patent No. ZL01256349.8 and Patent No. ZL200410066600.4. The above evidence was used to prove that the evidence submitted by the plaintiff, Quanneng Company, as the respondent, could not constitute a prior art defense, nor could it be a defense based on a later-filed patent application.

IV. Legal basis for the specific administrative act: Article 11, paragraph 1; Article 56, paragraph 1; and Article 57, paragraph 1 of the *Patent Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law).

The third party, Jia Dong Li Company, agreed with the opinion of the defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, and did not submit evidence.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court)

Patentees Ge Yongle, Li Jianjun, and Wang Taisheng filed an invention patent application on September 2, 2005, titled "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners," which was granted by the State Intellectual Property Office on November 7, 2007, under Patent No. ZL200510029351.6, and is currently a valid patent.

The claims of the "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" invention patent (hereinafter referred to as the patent in suit) set forth the following independent claim:
"1. An energy-saving atomizing device for a split-type air conditioner, the split-type air conditioner consisting of an indoor unit and an outdoor unit, characterized in that the atomizing device is additionally installed on the outdoor unit of the air conditioner, and the atomizing liquid produced by the atomizing device is sprayed onto the surface of the condenser to form evaporative cooling, thereby reducing the condensation temperature of the condenser; the atomizing device consists of a micro-motor and an atomizing disc connected to the main shaft of the motor; the atomizing disc is disc-shaped; and the atomizing surface of the atomizing disc is provided with dense radial or spiral concave-convex grooves or raised points."

On November 18, 2007, the said patentees entered into an exclusive implementation license contract with the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, for the patent in suit. Jia Dong Li Company became the exclusive licensee of the patent right, and the contract was filed with the State Intellectual Property Office on August 18, 2008.

On July 21, 2008, the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, purchased a product named "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" from the plaintiff, Quanneng Company, and the plaintiff issued an invoice. Both the product and its packaging bore the words "Shanghai Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd." and the model number RSW5000A. The components of the product included: a mounting bracket and a support secured to the mounting bracket; one end of the support was connected to a micro-motor, and the rotating shaft of the micro-motor was connected to an atomizing disc; between the micro-motor and the atomizing disc, there was a water inlet pipe and a water outlet pipe, with the water outlet pipe corresponding to the inner cavity of the atomizing disc; the atomizing disc was disc-shaped, and its surface was provided with dense radial concave-convex grooves. The product instruction manual stated that it could be used for split-type air conditioners and was an atomizing energy-saving device installed on the outdoor unit of the air conditioner, producing atomized liquid sprayed onto the condenser surface to form mixed air cooling and atomizing cooling, thereby reducing the condensation temperature and condensation pressure of the condenser.

On February 2, 2007, non-party Rongsheng Company filed a utility model patent application titled "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer," which was granted by the State Intellectual Property Office on January 2, 2008, under Patent No. ZL200720106248.1. On February 1, 2007, the same company filed a design patent application titled "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer," which was granted on January 16, 2008, under Patent No. ZL200730110936.0.

On September 17, 2008, the defendant, the Shanghai IP Bureau, received a request from Jia Dong Li Company for mediation of patent infringement. In its request, the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, claimed that the plaintiff, Quanneng Company, had, without the permission of the patentee, manufactured and sold a product named "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" (model RSW5000A), infringing the legitimate rights and interests of Jia Dong Li Company as the exclusive licensee, and requested the Shanghai IP Bureau to order Quanneng Company to immediately cease the infringement and stop manufacturing and selling the infringing product, and to mediate compensation for Jia Dong Li Company's economic losses and reasonable expenses such as attorney fees. The Shanghai IP Bureau accepted the case on September 22, 2008, and issued a notice of defense to Quanneng Company on the same day. After receiving the notice of defense on September 26, 2008, Quanneng Company submitted a statement of defense on October 3 of the same year. On the same day, the Shanghai IP Bureau issued oral hearing notices to both Jia Dong Li Company and Quanneng Company. On November 12, 2008, the Shanghai IP Bureau conducted an oral hearing, with representatives from both Jia Dong Li Company and Quanneng Company attending. On June 19, 2009, the Shanghai IP Bureau made the Decision on Handling Patent Infringement Dispute No. Huzhiju Chuzi [2008] No. 22, finding that the "Air Conditioner Energy-Saving Atomizer" product (hereinafter referred to as the allegedly infringing product) manufactured and sold by Quanneng Company completely covered the scope of protection of the invention patent right for the "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" (Patent No. ZL200510029351.6), infringing the legitimate rights and interests of Jia Dong Li Company, the exclusive licensee of that invention patent right. Pursuant to Article 11, paragraph 1, Article 56, paragraph 1, and Article 57, paragraph 1 of the *Patent Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Bureau ordered Quanneng Company to immediately cease its infringement of the invention patent right titled "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" (Patent No. ZL200510029351.6). The decision was served on both parties.

Disputed Issues at First Instance:
The disputed issues at first instance in this case were whether the facts found by the challenged patent infringement dispute handling decision, namely that the plaintiff, Quanneng Company's, manufacture and sale of the allegedly infringing product infringed the legitimate rights and interests of the third party, Jia Dong Li Company, were clear, and whether the law was correctly applied.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court)

I. The third party, Jia Dong Li Company, was the exclusive licensee of the patent in suit.
On November 18, 2007, the third party, through an exclusive implementation license contract entered into with the patentees of the "Energy-Saving Atomizing Device for Air Conditioners" (Patent No. ZL200510029351.6) invention patent, became the exclusive licensee of that invention patent right and enjoyed the corresponding rights and interests in that invention patent.

II. The technical features of the allegedly infringing product are identical to the essential technical features of the patent-in-suit. Upon comparing the technical features of the allegedly infringing product with the essential technical features of the patent-in-suit, both pertain to the same technical subject matter, i.e., an energy-saving atomization device for a split-type air conditioner, wherein the split-type air conditioner consists of an indoor unit and an outdoor unit; the atomization device is installed on the outdoor unit of the air conditioner, and the atomized liquid produced by the atomization device is sprayed onto the surface of the condenser to form evaporative cooling, thereby reducing the condensing temperature of the condenser; the atomization device is composed of a micro motor and an atomization disk mounted on the motor spindle; the atomization disk is disc-shaped, with dense radial concave-convex grooves on the surface of the atomization disk of the allegedly infringing product, while the atomization disk of the invention patent-in-suit is provided with dense radial or spiral concave-convex grooves or protrusions on its surface. In summary, the technical features of the allegedly infringing product are identical to the essential technical features of the invention patent-in-suit, and the allegedly infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the invention patent-in-suit.

III. The prior art defense of the plaintiff, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., is not established. To prove that the allegedly infringing product was manufactured based on prior art, the plaintiff submitted 44 patent documents during the patent administrative procedure and provided 23 patent documents in the administrative litigation of this case. Among the 44 patent documents submitted in the patent administrative procedure, 42 relate to technologies used in the field of agricultural spraying, rather than the technology of an atomization device installed on the outdoor unit of a split-type air conditioner; the remaining two patent documents, with patent numbers ZL01256349.8 and ZL200410066600.4, although related to air conditioning technology, do not involve the structure of the atomization device. Therefore, the relevant evidence submitted by the plaintiff in the patent administrative procedure cannot support its prior art defense.

Among the 23 patent documents provided by the plaintiff, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., in the administrative litigation of this case, two documents, namely Evidence 18 and Evidence 23 in the plaintiff's second set of evidence, concern utility model patents whose publication dates are later than the filing date of the patent-in-suit; nine documents, namely Evidence 1-6 and Evidence 19-21 in the plaintiff's second set of evidence, relate to technologies in the field of agricultural spraying; the remaining twelve documents, namely Evidence 7-17 and Evidence 22 in the plaintiff's second set of evidence, relate to air conditioner technology. Upon analysis and comparison, Evidence 7-10, 13, 16, 17, and 22 do not disclose the structure of the atomization disk or the technical feature that the atomization disk is driven by a motor; the atomization technologies disclosed in Evidence 11 and 12 differ from the structural features of the atomization disk of the plaintiff's allegedly infringing product; Evidence 14 does not disclose the technical solution of atomizing condensate water to reduce the condenser temperature; Evidence 15 involves a different technical subject matter, addressing the issue of air conditioning and humidification, and adopts a technical solution different from that of the plaintiff's allegedly infringing product. In summary, none of the 23 patent documents provided by the plaintiff can prove that the technology used in the allegedly infringing product constitutes prior art. Therefore, the plaintiff's prior art defense is not established.

In conclusion, the defendant, the Municipal Intellectual Property Bureau (hereinafter "the IP Bureau"), found that the plaintiff, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., without the permission of the patentee, manufactured and sold the allegedly infringing product for the purpose of production and operation, thereby infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., and ordered the plaintiff to immediately cease the infringement. The facts were clearly found and the applicable law was correctly applied. The challenged specific administrative act shall be upheld according to law. The plaintiff's claims and grounds for the lawsuit are not sustainable.

Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 11(1), Article 56(1), and Article 57(1) of the Patent Law (as amended on August 25, 2000), and Article 54(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 24, 2009:

The decision of the defendant, the IP Bureau, in the case of patent infringement dispute (Shanghai Intellectual Property Bureau Disposition [2008] No. 22) dated June 19, 2009, is upheld.

The court acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by the plaintiff, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.

Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court, with the main grounds: its manufactured and sold "Energy-Saving Atomizer for Air Conditioner" has obtained two patents, making it a lawfully produced product. If the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., considers it infringing, it might involve the revocation of its patents and thus should be accepted by the State Intellectual Property Office; its product is not the same as the third party's "Energy-Saving Atomization Device for Air Conditioner" but uses a more advanced motor, and both products are manufactured using prior art, so it does not infringe on the third party's rights. It requested the appellate court to reverse the judgment and revoke the challenged administrative decision.

The appellee, the IP Bureau, argued: The invention patent-in-suit of the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., is currently valid and effective. The technical features of the allegedly infringing product of the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., completely cover all the technical features recorded in the claims of the invention patent-in-suit. The appellant failed to prove that its product was manufactured based on prior art, thus constituting infringement. It requested the appellate court to affirm the original judgment.

The third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., submitted: The product of the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., infringed on its invention patent, and requested the appellate court to affirm the original judgment.

Upon trial of the second instance, the Shanghai High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Shanghai High People's Court held in the second instance:

Article 57(1) of the Patent Law (as amended on August 25, 2000) provides: "Where, without the permission of the patentee, any person exploits the patent, thereby infringing the patent right, and a dispute arises, the parties shall settle the dispute through negotiation; where the parties are unwilling to negotiate or fail to reach an agreement, the patentee or an interested party may institute legal proceedings in a People's Court, or may request the administrative authority for patent affairs to handle the matter. When the administrative authority for patent affairs handles the matter, if it finds that the infringement is established, it may order the infringer to immediately cease the infringement. Where the parties are dissatisfied, they may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notification of the handling, institute legal proceedings in a People's Court in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Where the infringer neither institutes legal proceedings within the prescribed time limit nor ceases the infringement, the administrative authority for patent affairs may request the People's Court to enforce the decision." The third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., became the exclusive licensee of the invention patent-in-suit by entering into an exclusive license agreement with the patentee and enjoys corresponding rights and interests. Therefore, the third party, believing that the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., manufactured and sold the allegedly infringing product, infringing its protected rights and interests, applied to the appellee, the IP Bureau, for a decision ordering cessation of infringement and mediation on compensation. The appellee accepted the application, conducted an oral hearing, heard the statements and defenses of the third party and the appellant, and, after the parties failed to reach a mediation agreement on compensation, issued the challenged administrative decision. The appellee had the corresponding authority to act, and the enforcement procedure was in compliance with the above legal provisions and was not improper. The appellant's claim that this case might involve the revocation of its patent and should be handled by the State Intellectual Property Office reflects a misunderstanding of the above legal provisions and the matters handled by the appellee, is clearly untenable, and is not accepted.

Article 11(1) of the Patent Law provides: "After the grant of a patent right for an invention or utility model, except as otherwise provided for in this Law, no entity or individual may, without the permission of the patentee, exploit the patent, that is, may not manufacture, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product, or use the patented process, or use, offer to sell, sell, or import the product directly obtained by the patented process, for production or business purposes." Article 56(1) provides: "The scope of protection of the patent right for an invention or utility model shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and the drawings may be used to interpret the claims." Therefore, whether the technical features of the allegedly infringing product completely cover all the technical features recorded in the claims of the invention patent-in-suit determines whether the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., infringes the patent right of the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd. The appellant claims that its product also obtained a patent right and therefore does not constitute infringement. Since the filing date of the invention patent-in-suit of Jiadongli Co., Ltd. is earlier than the filing dates of the utility model patent and design patent claimed by Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., in accordance with the principle of first-to-file under the Patent Law, the scope of protection of the earlier filed patent right of the third party should be used to examine whether the appellant's allegedly infringing product constitutes infringement. The utility model patent and design patent claimed by the appellant with later filing dates are irrelevant to whether the appellant's manufactured and sold allegedly infringing product infringes the invention patent-in-suit. Therefore, this claim of the appellant cannot be sustained.

Upon examination at trial, the claims of the invention patent-in-suit are: "1. An energy-saving atomization device for a split-type air conditioner, the split-type air conditioner consisting of an indoor unit and an outdoor unit, characterized in that the atomization device is installed on the outdoor unit of the air conditioner, the atomized liquid produced by the atomization device is sprayed onto the surface of the condenser to form evaporative cooling, thereby reducing the condensing temperature of the condenser, the atomization device is composed of a micro motor and an atomization disk mounted on the motor spindle, the atomization disk is disc-shaped, and the atomization surface of the atomization disk is provided with dense radial or spiral concave-convex grooves or protrusions." From the physical product and instruction manual of the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., it can be seen that the allegedly infringing product involves an energy-saving atomization device for a split-type air conditioner, wherein the split-type air conditioner consists of an indoor unit and an outdoor unit; the atomization device is installed on the outdoor unit of the air conditioner, the atomized liquid produced by the atomization device is sprayed onto the surface of the condenser to form evaporative cooling, thereby reducing the condensing temperature of the condenser; the atomization device is composed of a micro motor and an atomization disk mounted on the motor spindle; the atomization disk is disc-shaped, with dense radial concave-convex grooves on its surface. Clearly, the challenged administrative decision's finding that the allegedly infringing product completely covers all the technical features recorded in the claims of the invention patent-in-suit has corresponding factual and legal basis and is not improper. The appellant's ground of appeal that its product differs in name from the third party's product and uses more advanced technology, thus not constituting infringement, lacks legal basis and is not accepted.

The appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., in the administrative procedure and the original trial procedure, both claimed that the invention patent-in-suit of the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., was obtained based on "prior art" and that the appellant's product was also manufactured based on "prior art," as a defense against infringement. The appellant provided 44 and 23 patent specifications or extracts in the administrative procedure and the original trial procedure, respectively, to support its claim. From the analysis of the specifications, it is evident that these patents either involve the field of agricultural spraying, which is not the same technical field as the invention patent-in-suit and the allegedly infringing product, and the appellant did not prove that this technology could be directly used in the outdoor unit of a split-type air conditioner; or, although they involve air conditioner technology, some have publication dates later than the filing date of the invention patent-in-suit, some do not disclose the structure of the atomization disk, and some have structural principles different from those of the invention patent-in-suit and the allegedly infringing product. In this regard, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. must bear the adverse consequences of its failure to provide proof, and its prior art defense is not accepted.

In summary, the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., manufactured and sold the allegedly infringing product for the purpose of production and operation, which falls within the scope of protection of the invention patent-in-suit enjoyed by the third party, Jiadongli Co., Ltd., and constitutes infringement. The appellee, the IP Bureau, upon the application of the third party, after hearing the statements and defenses of both parties during the handling procedure, and after the parties failed to reach a mediation agreement on compensation, issued the challenged administrative decision, ordering the appellant to immediately cease the infringement. The facts were clearly found, the applicable law was correctly applied, and the enforcement procedure was lawful. The judgment of the original trial upholding the decision was not improper and shall be affirmed. The appeal of Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported. Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court, in accordance with Article 61(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on March 21, 2010:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The appellate case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by the appellant, Quanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.
